scope.topic: Mitosis: duplicated chromosome alignment and sister chromatid separation in eukaryotic cells
scope.organism_context: eukaryotic cells (animal cell examples with centrosomes/centrioles; plant/fungi differences noted but not modeled)
included_processes: prometaphase kinetochore attachment and chromosome orientation
metaphase alignment at the metaphase plate
anaphase sister chromatid separation and poleward movement
excluded_processes: prophase nuclear envelope breakdown and centrosome separation
simplifications: Only the alignment and separation of one duplicated chromosome is modeled; the full complement is not represented.
Molecular details of cohesin cleavage and motor protein activity are not modeled because the retrieved passages do not provide them.
Continuous mitotic events are represented as discrete processes for schematic clarity.
The model does not specify timing or duration of each process.

entities.scientific_name: duplicated chromosome (sister chromatid pair attached at centromere)

support.quote: the mechanisms that result in the formation of identical pairs of DNA molecules—sister chromatids—that are firmly attached at the centromeric region.
The sister chromatids are still tightly attached to each other by cohesin proteins.

states.attached: sister chromatids attached at centromere by cohesin

entities.scientific_name: kinetochore (protein structure at centromeric region of each sister chromatid)

support.quote: Each sister chromatid develops a protein structure called a kinetochore in the centromeric region

entities.scientific_name: mitotic spindle microtubule (kinetochore microtubule from a pole)

support.quote: The proteins of the kinetochore attract and bind mitotic spindle microtubules.
some of these microtubules come into contact with and firmly bind to the kinetochores.
all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate , or the equatorial plane, midway between the two poles of the cell.
the kinetochores of sister chromatids face the opposite poles.
the microtubules pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles.

relations.definition: Each kinetochore is a protein structure located at the centromeric region of a sister chromatid.

support.quote: Each sister chromatid develops a protein structure called a kinetochore in the centromeric region

relations.definition: Mitotic spindle microtubules from opposite poles bind to kinetochores of sister chromatids.

support.quote: The proteins of the kinetochore attract and bind mitotic spindle microtubules.
Eventually, all the sister chromatids will be attached via their kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.

relations.definition: During metaphase the duplicated chromosome is aligned at the metaphase plate.

support.quote: all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate , or the equatorial plane, midway between the two poles of the cell.

processes.scientific_name: prometaphase kinetochore microtubule attachment and chromosome orientation

preconditions.chromosome_condensed: Chromosomes become more condensed and discrete.
preconditions.kinetochore_formed: Each sister chromatid develops a kinetochore.
preconditions.spindle_microtubules_present: The mitotic spindle continues to develop as more microtubules assemble.

effects.attachment: Sister chromatids are attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.
effects.orientation: Chromosome is oriented until kinetochores of sister chromatids face opposite poles.

temporal_scope.start_condition: Kinetochores have formed on sister chromatids and spindle microtubules are present.
temporal_scope.end_condition: All sister chromatids of the chromosome are attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.

processes.scientific_name: metaphase alignment of chromosomes at the metaphase plate

preconditions.chromosome_attached_to_opposing_poles: Chromosome is attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.
preconditions.sister_chromatids_attached: Sister chromatids are still tightly attached to each other by cohesin proteins.

effects.alignment: All chromosomes are aligned in the metaphase plate.

temporal_scope.start_condition: Chromosome has achieved bipolar kinetochore attachment and is oriented.
temporal_scope.end_condition: Chromosome is aligned at the metaphase plate.

support.quote: all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate , or the equatorial plane, midway between the two poles of the cell.

processes.scientific_name: anaphase separation of sister chromatids and poleward movement

preconditions.metaphase_alignment: Chromosome aligned at the metaphase plate.
preconditions.bipolar_attachment: Sister chromatids attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.
preconditions.cohesin_present: Sister chromatids tightly attached by cohesin proteins.

effects.separation: The connection between sister chromatids breaks down.
effects.movement: Microtubules pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles.

temporal_scope.start_condition: Chromosome is aligned at the metaphase plate with sister chromatids attached to opposing poles.
temporal_scope.end_condition: Sister chromatids have separated and are being pulled toward opposite poles.

support.quote: During metaphase , the “change phase,” all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate , or the equatorial plane, midway between the two poles of the cell.
In anaphase, the connection between the sister chromatids breaks down, and the microtubules pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles.

precondition.bipolar_attachment: Sister chromatids attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.

the process of active division by which duplicated chromosomes (chromatids) attach to spindle fibers, align themselves along the equator of the cell, and then separate from each other.

unresolved_questions.question: The exact molecular mechanism by which the connection between sister chromatids breaks down (e.g., cohesin cleavage by separase) is not described in the retrieved passages.
The precise timing and duration of prometaphase, metaphase, and anaphase are not specified in the retrieved passages.
Whether the spindle assembly checkpoint is required for anaphase onset is not explicitly stated in the retrieved passages.
